# `mismatched-allocation-release`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports an allocation released with the wrong method or through a different
allocator.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`alloc`/`free` and `create`/`destroy` are distinct contracts, and allocator
identity must be preserved.

## When it fires

It applies when both acquisition and release receiver/method identities are
mechanically visible, including allocator values derived through `.allocator()`.
A helper returning a single-item pointer to an array (`*align(n) [n]u8`) from a
slice allocation may be released with either `destroy` or `free`. Only a receiver
that names an allocator counts as a different allocator: a wrapper method such as
`self.free(value)`, or a method of the owned value itself (`set.free(index)`), is
not compared.

It also reports an unmanaged container grown through one allocator parameter and
released through another, `list.append(a, x)` followed by `list.deinit(b)`. Only
parameters declared with an `Allocator` type are compared, since local bindings
may alias the same allocator, and a reassignment of the container ends the check.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn make(gpa: std.mem.Allocator) !void {
    const p = try gpa.create(u32);
    gpa.free(p);
}
```
